feedback: Written before this robot has raced, so no outcome is claimed. Evidence: iteration 5 (mass 0.5 kg, track 0.10 m) scored 422.9 with oval finish 95%, s-bend progress 0.72, and s-bend max_error at the 0.06 m limit (0.063). Iteration 6 (mass 0.4 kg) lowered s-bend progress to 0.59 and s-bend finishes to 2 of 20, so 0.5 kg is the right mass and should not go lower. The Builder's wheel_track 0.09 m raises effective steering gain by about 11%, and I have kept the iteration 5 controller unchanged, so the track change is the only variable. Depending on the next race: if s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m and steering_oscillation stays at or under 0.3, turn authority was the limit, so try wheel_track 0.08 m next. If s-bend max_error stays at about 0.06 m with steering_oscillation above 0.32, the controller gain is now the limit, and I will retune kp/kd on my side rather than change the geometry again. If slalom line_loss_events stay near 1.85 whatever the track does, sensor coverage is the limit, and the next geometry step is outer sensors at x = ±0.045 m. Iteration 1 showed that spread alone at y=0.04 m did not cut line losses, so that step is an untested hypothesis at y=0.07 m with 16 mm footprints.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration 5 mass of 0.5 kg and the 0.040 m wheel radius. Iteration 6 showed 0.4 kg lowers s-bend progress (0.72 to 0.59), and iteration 4 to 5 showed the radius gain lifts the oval finish rate.

If s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m with steering_oscillation at or under 0.3, try wheel_track 0.08 m (the allowed minimum) for more turn authority. Iteration 5 showed inertia reduction helped the bends, and this continues that trend.

If slalom line_loss_events stay at 1.85 or higher, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.045 m (x = -0.045, -0.0225, 0, 0.0225, 0.045) at y=0.07 m with the 16 mm footprint. This is an untested hypothesis: iteration 1 showed spread alone did not reduce line losses at y=0.04 m.
